title: Decayed z-score pop-affinity router with per-route escalation and variant quarantine
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Introduce an adaptive region selection service that fuses request-level latency quantiles (p50/p95) with a composite network health score (packet loss, jitter, retransmit rate) using a decayed z-score model. The goal is to reduce user-facing tail latency regressions while avoiding flip-flopping on transient noise and providing a structured quarantine for degraded model variants.
background: Current pop selection relies on raw percentile thresholds and short absolute windows which can cause oscillation during transient network events. There is no uniform penalty for stale telemetry or an aggregated statistical confidence signal across routes. Teams have observed increased p95 jitter during cross-pop incidents and unsafe rollbacks to lower-quality model variants when a single metric spikes.
goals: 1) Produce a single region affinity score per POP that combines p50/p95 deltas and nethealth in a statistically principled way (decayed z-score). 2) Add per-route escalation policies that weight region scores by route-specific SLAs and content type. 3) Implement a quarantine state for model variants that fail integrity checks (quality/regression anomalies) and for POPs with sustained nethealth penalty. 4) Provide observability and SLO alarms for the new signals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Router produces stable region choices with <5% flip rate during 10-minute transients in canary tests.
- p95 tail on sampled routes improves or stays within +/-5% of baseline during steady-state.
- Variant quarantine prevents traffic to flagged model versions for at least the configured cooling period.
- Dashboards expose decayed-zscore, nethealth, and quarantine events and are hooked into alerting rules.
design_decisions:
- Use rolling-window z-score where the mean and std carry an exponential decay (alpha) to emphasize recent telemetry but penalize too-fresh noisy reads.
- Combine latency z-score and nethealth with tunable weights per route (default: latency 0.7, nethealth 0.3).
- Nethealth composite = weighted sum of packet loss (pk_loss), jitter (ms_std), and retransmit ratio normalized into z-space.
- Staleness penalty: when a POP has telemetry older than 30s, apply an increasing penalty multiplier to the score.
- Hysteresis band: only switch POP if candidate score exceeds current by configurable margin (default 1.5 z).
- Variant quarantine: mark variant as QUARANTINED when model-internal quality checks + external error-rate exceed thresholds; quarantine decays after a minimum cool-off period (default 15m) with progressive probation traffic.
telemetry_spec:
- Inputs: per-POP request p50 and p95 (ms), sample counts, packet loss %, jitter std (ms), retransmit_rate %.
- Windows: short (1m EWMA), medium (5m decayed z baseline), long (1h baseline for seasonal).
- Decay alpha tunables: short_alpha=0.3, baseline_alpha=0.05.
- Confidence: use sample count to adjust z-score variance (low sample_count -> widen std).
- Emit metrics: pop.decayed_z_latency, pop.decayed_z_nethealth, pop.affinity_score, route.pop_choice_event with reason code, variant.quarantine_state.
algorithm_spec:
1) For each POP compute latency_z = (p95_current - baseline_mean_p95) / baseline_std_p95 where baseline values are EWMA with decay. 2) Compute nethealth_z similarly by normalizing the composite nethealth metric. 3) affinity_score = latency_weight * latency_z + nethealth_weight * nethealth_z. 4) Apply staleness_penalty = 1 + max(0, (age_seconds - 30))/30 capped at 3x. 5) final_score = affinity_score * (1 + staleness_penalty). 6) Route selection uses current_pop unless candidate final_score exceeds current_pop final_score + hysteresis_margin. 7) If candidate POP has variant.quarantine_state == QUARANTINED, suppress it unless no other POP available and apply safe-fallback policy.
Notes: z-scores must be clipped to reasonable range [-8, 8] to avoid overreaction to outliers.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Unit tests + offline replay against 72h trace of production telemetry (dev env). Phase 2: Shadow mode on non-prod routes for 2 days, collect flip-rate and score distribution. Phase 3: Gradual rollout to 10% traffic with canary traffic profiles (low/high-QPS). Phase 4: 50% after 48h of green metrics, then 100% with full observability and auto-rollback on safety triggers.
Rollback triggers: persistent >10% p95 regression for 1h, quarantine cascade affecting >3% of traffic, or error-rate >0.5% absolute increase.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for z-score calculations and staleness penalty.
- Replay tests: evaluate decisions versus baseline on historical incidents.
- Chaos tests: inject packet loss and jitter into one POP and assert controlled switchover without oscillation.
- Variant quarantine tests: synthetic quality regressions validate quarantine entry/exit and probation traffic ramp.
- Integration: verify dashboards and alert rules, smoke tests for route selection logic across regional tiers.
risks:
- Incorrect tuning could cause conservative behavior (stuck on degraded POP) or aggressive flips.
- Low sample routes may yield noisy z-scores despite confidence widening.
- Nethealth telemetry gaps could bias decisions; must guard with sane defaults.
- Interactions with autoscaling and Dedicated routing policies need coordination to avoid conflicting churn.
